background: The late Sadhuram Bansal set up a galvanised iron (GI) pipe unit in 1969, which the company describes as the first foundation of the Bansal group. Skipper was incorporated in Kolkata in 1981 (originally as Skipper Investments Ltd) and is run by his son Sajan Kumar Bansal. Sharan Bansal started the power transmission tower business in 2003 and built it into one of India's largest T&D structure makers; brothers Devesh and Siddharth later took telecom, railway and polymer pipe lines. Shares are held largely through four S.K. Bansal family trusts and family companies such as Skipper Plastics Ltd. Ram Gopal Bansal of BMW Industries is a director of Sadhuram Bansal & Sons Ltd, and press reports a split of a three-brother family business, so the two groups are likely branches of one family (not confirmed by filings).

background: BMW Industries was incorporated on 21 October 1981 as Bansal Mechanical Works Pvt Ltd and renamed BMW Industries Ltd in June 1999. Press reports say Ram Gopal Bansal started it with his two brothers as a family business; on the family separation he kept steel processing, while the brothers took pipes, tubes, poles and structures. Ram Gopal is still chairman, with sons Harsh and Vivek as joint MDs; the family also holds Sadhuram Bansal & Sons Ltd, which ties it to the Sadhuram Bansal (Skipper) family.

background: Vishambhar Saran is an engineer from Banaras Hindu University (1969) who spent about 33 years at Tata Steel, rising to Director of Raw Materials. He took voluntary retirement in March 1994 and founded the VISA group in April 1994; the name joins the first letters of Vishambhar and his wife Saroj, who already ran a firm called VISA Ltd in Kolkata. The group built a special steel and ferro chrome complex at Kalinganagar, Odisha, and spread into power, mining, trading, shipping and logistics. Heavy debt later forced the exit from special steel, and the listed company is now VISA Chrome (ferro chrome and coke), run by his son Vishal Agarwal.

background: The family started with a rolling mill in Howrah in 1974 and incorporated Beekay Steel Industries in Kolkata on 28 March 1981. It grew by buying Radice Ispat (India), which started a unit at Chengalpattu, Tamil Nadu in 1999, and AKC Steel Industries (1998), and opened TMT mills in Jamshedpur in 2001. Beekay makes hot rolled sections, bright bars, structurals and TMT bars and does conversion work for Tata Steel and others. Brothers Suresh Chand (Executive Chairman) and Mukesh Chand Bansal (Executive Director) run it with Suresh's sons Vikas and Manav and Mukesh's son Gautam. A family HUF in the name of B.L. Bansal suggests he was the father of the brothers (inferred).

background: Om Prakash Jalan has traded coke and coking coal since 1993 and knows the Chinese, Australian and Indian met coke markets. He set up Bengal Energy Ltd in May 2007 with Navin Maheshwari, a chartered accountant who handles day-to-day running (an earlier rating also named Rajeev Maheshwari). Its plant at Narayangarh, Paschim Medinipur, is one of eastern India's largest low-ash metallurgical (LAM) coke units (6 lakh tonnes a year), with pig iron, ferro alloys, iron ore pellets, sinter and waste-heat power added later. Revenue was about Rs 3,578 crore in FY2025. No family successors are named in rating reports.

The two share about eight directors, including Nandlal, Mukund and Siddharth Rungta, and press describes them as related companies of one group that mines iron ore and makes steel, mainly in Odisha and Jharkhand. Rungta Sons holds iron ore leases such as the Jhumka-Pathiriposhi West block in Jharkhand. Fortune India ranked Nandlal and Mukund Rungta 61st among India's richest, with about Rs 40,000 crore combined. This group is separate from the Jharkhand Rungta group of Ram Chandra, Alok and Abhishek Rungta (Aloke Steels, Araanya Mines); no filing links the two.
